# PilcrowMD test pack – Big file

**What this is.** A long document – about 2 MB and 1,508 chapters – made of ordinary
Markdown: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, code and a few formulas. It is here to test speed
and memory, not looks. The text is generated and does not mean anything.

**What to look for**

- **Opening.** Time how long it takes from tapping the file to seeing text. A few seconds is
  expected on a file this size; the app should not freeze or close.
- **Scrolling.** Fling up and down quickly. Scrolling should stay smooth, with no blank areas that
  stay blank.
- **Jumping.** Use the jump-to-bottom button, then jump back to the top.
- **Headings drawer.** It lists all 1,508 chapters. Tap one near the end.
- **Search.** Search for *quartermaster*: the first match is this line, the second is in the
  middle of the file. Search for *zebrafinch*: the second match is on the very last line. Then
  search for *harbour*, which appears thousands of times; the count should arrive without freezing
  the screen.
- **Edit.** Switch to Edit, scroll to the end, type a word, and save. Then reopen the file and
  check your word is there and nothing else changed.

**Known gaps in version 1.0.12** – we know about these, no need to report them:

- The reader prepares the whole document at once, on the screen's own thread. On a very large file
  the screen can freeze for a while, and Android may offer to close the app.
- Files of tens of megabytes can crash reading mode by running out of memory. This file is well
  below that size.
- Switching a very large file (tested at 32 MB) to Edit has closed the app once, with no error.
- A closed collapsible section that holds hundreds of blocks makes the file slower to open.
- Saving a file that uses Windows line endings does part of the work on the screen's thread, so a
  large file can stutter while it saves.
- In the Dark theme, a hard fling past the end of the file can turn the text area blank. Swipe back
  and the text returns.

If this file opens and scrolls well, a bigger one may still not. If you test a bigger file, please
tell us its size and what happened, at <https://github.com/pilcrowmd/pilcrow/issues>.
